name: Idli
funFact: Idli is a steamed rice cake that has been eaten in Tamil Nadu for over 1000 years, traditionally served as breakfast with sambar and coconut chutney.

name: Dosa
funFact: Dosa is a fermented crepe made from rice and lentils, a staple breakfast across Tamil Nadu and a UNESCO candidate for cultural heritage.

name: Sambar
funFact: Sambar is a lentil-based vegetable stew that is the soul of Tamil cuisine, served with idli, dosa, and rice at every meal.

name: Rasam
funFact: Rasam is a thin, peppery tamarind soup traditionally consumed as a digestive aid. It is served in the middle of a Tamil meal to cleanse the palate.

name: Pongal
funFact: Pongal is the most important Tamil harvest festival dish, cooked in a clay pot until it overflows — symbolising abundance and prosperity.

name: Chettinad Chicken Curry
funFact: Chettinad cuisine from the Chettinad region uses rare spices like kalpasi (stone flower) and marathi mokku that are unique to this cooking tradition.

name: Puliyodarai
funFact: Puliyodarai (tamarind rice) is a sacred temple food offered as prasad at Tamil Nadu temples, especially during Karthigai Deepam festival.

name: Kozhukattai
funFact: Kozhukattai is a steamed rice dumpling offered to Lord Ganesha during the Vinayagar Chaturthi festival in Tamil Nadu.

name: Murukku
funFact: Murukku is a crunchy spiral snack made during Diwali and Krishna Jayanthi in Tamil homes. The word 'murukku' means twisted in Tamil.

name: Paruppu Payasam
funFact: Paruppu Payasam is a moong dal kheer made with jaggery, an essential sweet dish served at Tamil weddings and auspicious occasions.

name: Avial
funFact: Avial is a mixed vegetable dish with coconut and yogurt, said to have been invented by Bhima of the Mahabharata when he worked as a cook.

name: Mor Kuzhambu
funFact: Mor Kuzhambu is a buttermilk-based curry that is a staple summer food in Tamil Nadu, cooling the body in hot weather.

name: Vazhaipoo Vadai
funFact: Vazhaipoo Vadai uses banana blossom, a highly nutritious flower that is a traditional Tamil ingredient with medicinal properties.

name: Sundal
funFact: Sundal is a boiled legume dish offered as prasad during the Navaratri festival, with a different legume made each of the nine days.

name: Thayir Sadam
funFact: Curd rice is the final course of a traditional Tamil meal and is considered sacred — it is said to cool the body, mind, and soul.

name: Kothu Parotta
funFact: Kothu Parotta is a street food icon of Tamil Nadu — shredded flaky flatbread stir-fried on a hot griddle with egg and spicy gravy.

name: Keerai Masiyal
funFact: Keerai Masiyal is a mashed spinach dish that has been a part of the Tamil diet for centuries, eaten with rice and ghee.

name: Nei Choru
funFact: Nei Choru (ghee rice) is a festive rice dish from Tamil Nadu often served at weddings and temple festivals with kurma or salna.

name: Thakkali Sadam
funFact: Thakkali Sadam is a tangy tomato rice loved by Tamil school children as a tiffin box staple and a quick weekday lunch.

name: Kadala Curry
funFact: Black chickpea curry cooked in Kerala-Tamil style with roasted coconut gravy, traditionally served with puttu on Sunday mornings.

name: Hyderabadi Mutton Biryani
funFact: Hyderabadi Biryani uses the dum cooking technique where meat and rice are slow-cooked together in a sealed vessel over charcoal.

name: Kerala Fish Curry
funFact: Kerala Fish Curry is made with kudampuli (Gambooge) giving it a unique sour flavour unlike any other Indian fish curry.

name: Butter Chicken
funFact: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani) was invented accidentally in Delhi in the 1950s by mixing leftover tandoori chicken in tomato cream sauce.

name: Dal Makhani
funFact: Dal Makhani is slow-cooked overnight on a tandoor, giving it a rich creamy texture. It is one of India's most iconic restaurant dishes.

name: Palak Paneer
funFact: Palak Paneer is a creamy spinach curry with fresh cheese, one of the most internationally recognised Indian vegetarian dishes.

name: Pizza Margherita
funFact: Pizza Margherita was created in 1889 in Naples for Queen Margherita of Italy, with toppings in the colours of the Italian flag.

name: Sushi Nigiri
funFact: Nigiri sushi originated in Tokyo (then Edo) in the early 19th century as a fast street food served from outdoor stalls.

name: Pad Thai
funFact: Pad Thai was promoted by the Thai government in the 1930s as a national dish to encourage rice noodle consumption and build national identity.

name: Chocolate Mousse
funFact: Chocolate mousse was first introduced in France in the 1750s and means 'foam' in French, referring to its light airy texture.

name: Chicken 65
funFact: Chicken 65 was invented at Hotel Buhari in Chennai in 1965. It is one of the most popular Tamil Nadu starters, served as a bar snack and party appetizer.

name: Filter Coffee
funFact: South Indian filter coffee brewed in a traditional brass filter is a ritual in Tamil homes — served frothy in a davara-tumbler set.

name: Appam (Tamil Nadu)
funFact: Appam is a lacy, bowl-shaped rice pancake made from fermented batter, traditionally paired with coconut milk or vegetable stew.

name: Chettinad Egg Curry
funFact: Chettinad Egg Curry uses a bold spice blend from the Chettinad region including kalpasi and dried red chillies for an intense flavour.

name: Kappa Biryani
funFact: Kappa Biryani is a beloved Kerala dish of tapioca mixed with spiced fish curry, popular in the Tamil Nadu-Kerala border belt districts.

name: Vada Curry
funFact: Vada Curry is a Chennai invention — crumbled chana dal vadas simmered in a spicy onion-tomato gravy, served exclusively with parotta or idiyappam.

name: Appam
funFact: Appam is a bowl-shaped rice pancake with a soft, spongy center and crispy lacy edges, traditionally paired with coconut milk stew in Kerala.

name: Puttu
funFact: Puttu is a steamed cylindrical cake of rice flour and coconut, a beloved Kerala breakfast traditionally eaten with kadala curry or banana.

name: Pesarattu
funFact: Pesarattu is a green moong dal crepe unique to Andhra Pradesh, high in protein and typically served with ginger chutney and upma.

name: Bisi Bele Bath
funFact: Bisi Bele Bath means 'hot lentil rice dish' in Kannada. It is Karnataka's iconic one-pot comfort meal, traditionally served with ghee and pappadums.

name: Pav Bhaji
funFact: Pav Bhaji originated in Mumbai in the 1850s as a quick meal for textile mill workers — mashed vegetables cooked with butter and spices, served with soft bread rolls.

name: Chole Bhature
funFact: Chole Bhature is a celebrated Punjabi street food pairing spicy chickpea curry with deep-fried fluffy bread — a Sunday breakfast favourite across North India.

name: Kootu
funFact: Kootu is a thick Tamil Nadu dish combining vegetables and lentils with a freshly ground coconut spice paste — a staple in every Tamil home's weekly menu.

name: Pani Puri
funFact: Pani Puri is one of India's most beloved street foods — hollow crispy shells filled with spiced potatoes and dunked in tangy mint-tamarind water.

name: Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
funFact: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani was developed in the Nizam's royal kitchens in the 18th century. The 'dum' (slow-cooking under sealed dough) method is its defining technique.
